---
title: "Olympic Trends"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/data-prep.R")

medal_timeline_data <- beach_medals |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(year, levels = sort(unique(year))),
    country = factor(country, levels = rev(country_medal_totals$country)),
    hover_text = paste0(
      country,
      "<br>Event: ", gender,
      "<br>Olympic year: ", year,
      "<br>Medal: ", medal
    )
  )

beach_age_records <- beach_athletes |>
  mutate(
    country = coalesce(country, "Country unavailable in source"),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", name, "</b>",
      "<br>Olympic year: ", year,
      "<br>Event: ", gender,
      "<br>Age: ", age,
      "<br>Country: ", country
    )
  )
```

## Every team medal, from Atlanta to Paris

Each point is one medal-winning country-team. Compare the men's and women's podiums across all eight Games; hover for the country, team, year, and medal.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "All 48 beach-volleyball team medals, one point per podium team. Source: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for 2020 and 2024."

medal_timeline_chart <- ggplot(
  medal_timeline_data,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = country,
    color = medal,
    shape = gender,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.55),
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~gender, ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(Gold = "#c99837", Silver = "#9caab5", Bronze = "#b87950"),
    breaks = c("Gold", "Silver", "Bronze")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Olympic year",
    y = "Medal-winning country",
    color = "Medal",
    shape = "Event"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(color = "#355260"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "#294655"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#10384a"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#637780", hjust = 0)
  )

plotly::ggplotly(medal_timeline_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
Sources: `olympicAthletes` through 2016 and official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Each point is one of the **`r scales::comma(nrow(beach_medals))`** team-medal results.
:::

There are only 48 distinct Olympic beach-volleyball team medals across eight editions, so every podium team is shown instead of expanding medal totals into extra points.

## One Olympic timeline, three lenses

The broadest view follows every Summer Olympic athlete-event entry. The gold trace then zooms in: first on all indoor and beach **Volleyball** entries, then on beach volleyball alone, identified from the **event** field. Each panel has its own vertical scale so the specialist event remains visible.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Athlete-event entries at Summer Olympic Games. Panels use separate vertical scales."

ggplot(
  participation_by_year,
  aes(x = year, y = records, color = series, group = series)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.05) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~series, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "All Summer sport entries" = "#315d70",
      "Volleyball sport entries" = "#0e8292",
      "Beach volleyball event entries" = "#c99837"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(8)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Athlete-event records",
    color = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes.",
      scales::comma(summer_records_used),
      "Summer Games records aggregated; the dataset contains",
      scales::comma(source_records),
      "records overall."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#10384a"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(color = "#355260"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#637780", hjust = 0)
  )
```

Because each panel has its own vertical scale, compare the shape of the trends rather than their heights across panels. Beach volleyball entries first appear in 1996 (84 athlete-event rows) and reach 96 in 2000, where they remain through 2024.

## Athlete ages across the Games

These points show individual beach-volleyball athlete-event records, not yearly averages. The spread reveals the age range within each event and how it changes across editions.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Each point is one of 756 beach-volleyball athlete-event records from 1996–2024. Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes."

age_timeline_chart <- ggplot(
  beach_age_records,
  aes(
    x = age,
    y = year,
    color = gender,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.62) +
  facet_wrap(~gender, ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Men = "#147f91", Women = "#c99837")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(beach_age_records$year))) +
  labs(
    x = "Athlete age (years)",
    y = "Olympic year",
    color = "Event"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#10384a"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#355260")
  )

plotly::ggplotly(age_timeline_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
Source: `olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes`; **`r scales::comma(nrow(beach_age_records))`** athlete-event rows from 1996–2024. Age is present for every beach-volleyball record in this source.
:::

Because each marker is a real athlete-event record, repeated appearances by the same athlete in different editions remain separate rows and are not synthetic extra observations.

::: {.callout-note}
## What counts as a record?

One row represents one athlete at one Games edition in one event—not one unique person or one team. Beach volleyball is filtered from `event` within the Volleyball sport, rather than treating all Volleyball entries as beach volleyball.
:::

The [Men vs. Women](men-vs-women.qmd) page focuses on beach volleyball participation and podiums by event.
